title: What is known about 1RB0RE_1LC1RA_1LD0LC_0RE0LA_1RA1RF_0RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_1LC1RA_1LD0LC_0RE0LA_1RA1RF_0RA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. A two-level counter on words 0 1^(odd): the run of 1s at the right end grows by 2 per round in doubling time while a carry moves left through the word; full rewrites at 1.7e6 and 2.6e7 steps; open.

Round 6, the proved neighbours. busycoq (pull request 36) proves the machines that differ from this one only in the entry D0. That entry is used from the first steps of this run and again and again (27 times in the first 1010 steps (10 in the first 103, 13 in 104, 14 in 105, 15 in 106, 25 in 107, 26 in 108, 27 in 1010)), and each use leaves a different left end than in the neighbours, so their proof does not carry over. No transfer; the question stays open.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 285 cells have been visited and 144 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Three rounds of the run, for any tape further left
claims.text: Three consecutive rounds of the run from blank tape (between moments the head is in A on the first 0 right of everything written), each proved for every tape left of the cells it visits, with its exact step count.

claims.title: What the entry D0 does, and the two halting patterns
claims.text: The entry fires when C, erasing 1s leftwards, reads a 0 with another 0 on its left: four steps later (C0, D0, E1, F0) the cells read 0 1 0 and A is on the next cell to the right. The machine halts from exactly two local patterns, each proved in Lean to halt whatever else is on the tape: B reading a 0 with two 0s on its left (0 0 B>0) and A reading 1 1 1. That there is no other way to halt is read backwards from the table (an argument on paper, not in Lean).

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>9</sup> steps; rebuilds
claims.text: Direct simulation. The fast counter is the run 1^(2k) at the right end: it grows by 2 per round, and each round takes twice as long as the one before plus about 2 steps (T′ = 2T + 2 in regular stretches). The slow list was rebuilt at about 1.66·106 and 2.55·107 steps; between rebuilds each round makes one local change in it.

claims.title: The entry D0 is used from the start and keeps being used
claims.text: In the run from blank tape the entry D0 is first used at step 4; 27 times in the first 1010 steps (10 in the first 103, 13 in 104, 14 in 105, 15 in 106, 25 in 107, 26 in 108, 27 in 1010). The proved neighbours use their version of the entry too (the neighbour with 1LB in the first machine's lettering: 11 times in 1010 steps), so the difference is not an unused entry: it changes the run.

claims.title: Two-level counter
claims.text: Left of the fast counter is a slow list, a word in a, b, c, d, e: blocks of odd length separated by single 0s. In each round one local change happens in it, a little further left each time (a carry: for example c a^3 → b a b a^2, b^3 → a^2 b^2), so the list behaves like the low digits of a slow counter whose digits are the odd block lengths. When the change reaches the left end, the head sweeps the whole tape: going left, state C erases runs of 1s and the tape is rewritten into words 1^2 0^k, and going right it is rewritten back, a rebuild that makes the list longer. This pair shares the first rows 1RB0RE_1LC1RA_1LD0LC and differs in D0 and E1; both behave in the same way. Not shown for all sizes.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. See the heuristic claims above for what a halt would need.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine is a two-level counter: a fast counter at the right end of the tape needs twice as long for each round, and each round makes one small change in a slow list of blocks on its left; rarely the slow list is rebuilt. This page runs the machine and shows the rounds.

facts.text: Rounds of the run proved in Lean for any tape further left.
Each round twice as long as the one before.

sections.heading: A fast counter and a slow list
html: Look at the tape each time the head is in state A on the first blank cell right of everything written. Read the tape as words a = 01, b = 0111, c = 011111, d = 0 1^7, e = 0 1^9 (a 0 followed by an odd run of 1s) and z = 00; a^4 is four a's. The fast counter is the run 1^(2k) at the right end: it grows by 2 per round, and each round takes twice as long as the one before plus about 2 steps (T′ = 2T + 2 in regular stretches).

sections.heading: Why it is hard to settle
html: The machine can halt only on its one undefined transition. The regular rounds are proved in Lean for three instances (for every tape further left) and behave the same way in every round seen; a halt could only come from a rebuild of the slow list (seen at about 1.66·106 and 2.55·107 steps). Rebuilds come after exponentially many rounds, and their rule is not known for all sizes, so the run cannot be followed beyond direct simulation. Since every rebuild seen made the list longer, the machine looks like it runs forever, but that is an extrapolation.

sections.heading: The proved neighbours
html: The community tracker notes: one table, three starts, one entry away from a machine proved in busycoq's pull request 36. This machine is the table of 1RB1RF_1RC0RA_1LD1RB_1LE0LD_0RA0LB_0RB--- started in that machine's state B (its states B, C, D, E, A, F are A, B, C, D, E, F here); a third holdout, 1RB0RA_0LC0RE_1LE1LD_0LE---_1LF0LC_1RA1LE, is the mirrored table from another start. The proved machines are 1RB0RE_1LC1RA_1LD0LC_1LA0LA_1RA1RF_0RA--- and 1RB0RE_1LC1RA_1LD0LC_1RA0LA_1RA1RF_0RA--- (D0 = 1LA, 1RA; here 0RE): the same table except for the entry D0.

The entry fires when C, erasing 1s leftwards, reads a 0 with another 0 on its left: four steps later (C0, D0, E1, F0) the cells read 0 1 0 and A is on the next cell to the right. In the neighbours the same moment writes a 1 there instead and carries on differently (to the left for 1L, to the right for 1R).

The entry is used 27 times in the first 1010 steps (10 in the first 103, 13 in 104, 14 in 105, 15 in 106, 25 in 107, 26 in 108, 27 in 1010). So the proof cannot be carried over by showing the entry is never reached. The neighbours' proofs are long inductions over a word-and-counter description of each machine's own run (about 1,200 to 1,700 lines of Coq each); they depend on what this entry leaves at the left end of the word, and we did not find a replacement invariant for this machine. The tracker says the same in its own words: the rare entry keeps changing the head of the word.
What Lean adds here is small: the effect of the entry, and the two local patterns from which the machine halts (B reading a 0 with two 0s on its left (0 0 B>0); A reading 1 1 1).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.048).
After 109 steps the tape spans 285 cells (24 left of the start, 258 right), with a density of 1s of 0.505.

summary: A two-level counter on words 0 1^(odd): the run of 1s at the right end grows by 2 per round in doubling time while a carry moves left through the word; full rewrites at 1.7e6 and 2.6e7 steps; open. One entry (D0) away from machines proved in busycoq; the entry is used again and again, so that proof does not transfer.
